contexts.text: The Angels urged Lot to haste () = that the Lord withheld them from evil, and kept them in good. To haste, and to urge = to urge...
What is this that thou hast hasted to find, my son? () = production so hasty.
An eagle hasting to devour () = to desolate man as to truths.

God hasteth to do it () = with every event... To haste, or haste, in the internal sense, is not quickly; but it is what is certain, and also what is full; thus with every event; for haste involves time; and in the Spiritual World there is no time, but instead of time there is state; thus the haste of time there relates to a corresponding quality of state; and the quality of state which corresponds is that there are a number of things which are together efficient, from which results a certain and full event.
Joseph hasted () = from the inmost. To haste, here, = that which breaks forth from the inmost. Explained.
They hasted () = impatience. To haste, when they are in the ardour of exculpating themselves, = impatience.
Wherefore have ye hasted to come today? () = perception that now conjunction is certain... To haste to come = certain conjunction. To haste = what is certain.
Pharaoh hasted to call Moses and Aaron () = fear then on account of truth from the Divine. To haste = from fear; for all haste comes forth from some affection which is excited.
And ye shall eat it in haste () = the affection of separation. Haste = affection, because it is of affection.
Egypt was urgent upon the people in hasting to send them out of the land () = that from aversion and fear they urged them to depart.
For whatever is done not tardily, but hastily, is done from the affection of love.
I will not drive him out from before thee in one year = no hasty flight or removal of the... falsities and evils signified by the nations in the Land of Canaan.
A deficiency... and but little spiritual life, if the removal should be hasty. Signified.
When man is being regenerated... he is regenerated not hastily, but slowly. Explained.
That a hasty removal of evils and falsities causes a rushing in of falsities from these loves. Explained.

Moses hastened, and bowed himself to the earth, and adored () = reception then from influx into the external, and worship from humiliation. To haste = affection; here, reception by means of influx and also reception by man therein.
Dangers... from a too great hastening of the time of betrothals.
By swift and haste, in the Word, is signified what is excited by affection and desire. AE 355:27.
